policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly reads the plural 'their sisters,' distinguishing the qere וְאַחְיוֹתֵיהֶם from the ketiv ואחיתיהם.

ASV's relative clause 'that dwelt at Jabez' can represent either the qere participial יֹשְׁבֵי or the ketiv finite ישבו, and no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them; the base qere therefore remains the fallback.
